---
title: "Design notes"
---

Why the robot is built the way it is and latest changes

## Log of 2026 changes
- Front of gears: exactly 1 mm spacing for washer. Back of gears (towards tail) has builtin 3D-printed spacers that press against inner bearing. Printing them will not use support
- All 3D printed cross fixing is now done with M2 square half nuts (stainless). Takes less space and less work than heat inserts. 3D printed plates are all 4 mm thick.
- Tail tube is now 5/3 round instead of square. The bracket (tail rigidifier) adapted in consequence.
- Left gear extended and wraps around the linkage for better support. 
- Crank-link shaft is now 10.5 mm to have enough space to fit a circlip. 
- Linkage bearings are now 4x10x4 on input and 3x8x4 on output. MAX static loading of 130 N.
- ESC box is now screwed against right bearing holder
- Front dome mounts to front plate
- Micro-controller box: to be printed transparent, no more window. Square nut assembly. USB-C port sits closer to edge of part, should give a better connection to program. 
- Gear shafts bearings changed to 3x7x3 flanged, with the flange now inserting into part. 
- All parts relabeled


## Gearbox corrosion {#gearbox-corrosion}
By default the gearbox on the FAAV4 is not waterproof at all, and it is normal
for it to fill completely with water once submerged. This is considered
acceptable: over more than a year of repeated use in water, including in lakes, a gearbox was opened and showed no sign of corrosion.

Proper lubrication: a mix of
**CorrosionX and white lithium grease** - help with corrosion problems. The practical procedure is in
[Module 10](/sessions/10-waterproofing.qmd).
